name: tile-band
title: Tile band
description: A band of hand-painted tiles for a border or a section divider: Goan azulejo, the blue-and-white tiles of the Portuguese-era houses and churches, with a majolica sister in cobalt, lemon yellow and leaf green. Four geometric and floral motifs (a rosette, a quatrefoil, quarter-circle corners, a vine) laid from a seed, painted once on a canvas and kept, crisp at any pixel ratio, running along the page or down it. Quiet is a cobalt hairline, flat; warm is a hand-painted glaze with brush variation and crackle; playful turns a tile a quarter when you touch it, and settles.

motif.gloss: Azulejo: the painted tiles of Goa's Portuguese-era houses and churches; majolica is its Mediterranean cousin.

budget.reason: Decision 0005 and 0010: element 12 KB, pure core 12 KB apart, skins 8 KB each with a shared helper counting as one. Today about 25.5 KB: element 2.0 KB, pure core 11.0 KB (four motifs as path data, the seeded laying, crackle, the turn), the canvas manager 6.5 KB and the painter 5.2 KB, three one-line skins. It is a component, not a scene, because its box is the band (a length and a thickness the page chooses, horizontal or vertical) and it has no loop: it is painted once, and a rAF runs only for the half second of a turn.
